hints.title: Monotonic Score Property
hints.text: For non-negative elements, shrinking a subarray decreases both its sum and its length, thus monotonically decreasing its score.

hints.title: Two-Pointer Sliding Window
hints.text: For each right endpoint r, advance the left pointer L until subarray score sum * (r - L + 1) < k.

hints.title: Subarray Counting Formula
hints.text: When valid, all subarrays ending at r starting from L to r are valid, adding r - L + 1 to total.

hints.title: Sliding Window Subarray Score Count Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def countSubarrays(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        left = 0
        running_sum = 0
        ans = 0
        for right in range(len(nums)):
            running_sum += nums[right]
            while running_sum * (right - left + 1) >= k:
                running_sum -= nums[left]
                left += 1
            ans += (right - left + 1)
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Both pointers move from 0 to n in a single pass.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all O(n^2) subarrays takes quadratic time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate uses monotonic score property to frame the problem as a standard two-pointer sliding window.
